def: A communication call involving a whole group of GPUs, such as all-reduce, reduce-scatter or all-gather.
A collective after which every GPU holds the element-wise sum (or average) of the tensors all GPUs started with.
A collective that sums tensors across GPUs but leaves each GPU holding only its own slice of the result.
A collective in which each GPU contributes a slice and afterwards every GPU holds the full concatenation.
Training with a full copy of the model on every GPU, each processing a different slice of the batch, with gradients averaged across GPUs.
The Zero Redundancy Optimizer: data parallelism that shards optimiser state, then gradients, then weights across GPUs instead of replicating them.
Fully Sharded Data Parallel, PyTorch's implementation of the ZeRO-3 idea, in which each GPU stores a shard of everything and gathers weights layer by layer.
Splitting each layer's weight matrices across GPUs so that they compute one layer together, at the cost of all-reduces inside every layer.
Splitting a model's layers into consecutive stages on different GPUs and streaming micro-batches through them.
The idle time of pipeline stages at the start and end of a step, equal to (p-1)/(m+p-1) of the schedule for p stages and m micro-batches.
Splitting activations along the sequence dimension in the parts of a layer that tensor parallelism leaves replicated, to save memory without extra traffic.
Splitting the input sequence across GPUs for the whole model, including attention, to train on very long sequences.
A small slice of a batch processed in one forward and backward pass, used to fill a pipeline or to accumulate gradients.
